## Summary: What's New and Different with Babylon Lite

**Babylon Lite** is a ground-up reimagining of the Babylon.js engine, designed from scratch for the modern web. Here are the key differences and new features:

### Core Philosophy
- **Minimal size & maximum performance first** — unlike Babylon.js which optimizes for broad usability and backward compatibility, Lite prioritizes bundle size and runtime performance above all else.
- **Not a replacement** — the two engines coexist side-by-side. Lite is for when you need the smallest bundle and highest performance; Babylon.js is for the broadest feature set and backward compatibility.

### Major Architectural Differences

| Aspect | Babylon.js | Babylon Lite |
|---|---|---|
| **Rendering API** | WebGL 1/2 + WebGPU | **WebGPU-only** — no WebGL fallback |
| **API Style** | Class-based OOP (`new Scene(engine)`) | **Plain data + functions** (`createSceneContext(engine)`) |
| **Tree-shaking** | Partial | **100% tree-shakable** — unused features cost zero bytes |
| **Scene ownership** | Objects know about the scene | **Scene is sole owner** — objects are standalone data, added via `addToScene()` |
| **Bundle size** | Large (hundreds of KB to MB) | **Fraction of Babylon.js** — measured per-scene with strict KB ceilings |
| **Build toolchain** | Various | **Vite-only** with WGSL shader minification |

### Key Technical Features
- **Frame Graph** — explicit ordered render tasks (RenderPass, RTT, overlays) instead of implicit rendering
- **Node Material Editor support** — NME snippet parser covering core, PBR, math, texture, procedural blocks
- **WGSL shaders** — all shaders written in WGSL, minified in production builds
- **Dynamic imports** — features like animation groups, PBR reflectance, etc. are only loaded when actually used
- **Pixel-identical output** — validated via Playwright visual parity tests with golden reference screenshots against Babylon.js
- **189 demo scenes** with parity tests proving visual equivalence

### Three Packages
1. **`babylon-lite`** — The core engine library (the main product)
2. **`@babylonjs/lite-compat`** — An opt-in **compatibility layer** that provides Babylon.js-shaped APIs (`new Scene()`, `new Camera()`, etc.) on top of Lite, as a migration runway. Unsupported APIs throw `LiteCompatError` so gaps are discoverable.
3. **`babylon-lite-gl`** — Placeholder for potential future WebGL support

### What's Intentionally NOT Supported (🚫)
- WebGL 1.0 / 2.0
- Classic `InstancedMesh` API (use thin instances instead)
- Full particle systems, audio, GUI, inspector, node editor
- Many Babylon.js plugins (AmmoJS, CannonJS, OBJ/STL/FBX loaders, etc.)

### What Lite Does Support Well
- PBR materials (metallic-roughness, specular-glossiness, clearcoat, sheen, anisotropy, subsurface)
- Standard materials, ShaderMaterial, GridMaterial
- glTF/.babylon/.hdr/.dds loaders + KTX/Basis compressed textures
- Shadows (ESM, PCF, cascaded)
- Skeleton animation, morph targets, vertex animation textures
- Havok Physics V2, Recast V2 navigation
- Gaussian splatting (.ply, .splat, .sog, .spz)
- CSG operations, picking, post-processing
- Device-lost recovery
- Post-process pipeline (bloom, SSAO, FXAA, DOF, chromatic aberration, etc.)

## Summary: What's New and Different with Babylon Lite

**Babylon Lite** is a ground-up reimagining of the Babylon.js engine, designed from scratch for the modern web. Here are the key differences and new features:

### Core Philosophy
- **Minimal size & maximum performance first** — unlike Babylon.js which optimizes for broad usability and backward compatibility, Lite prioritizes bundle size and runtime performance above all else.
- **Not a replacement** — the two engines coexist side-by-side. Lite is for when you need the smallest bundle and highest performance; Babylon.js is for the broadest feature set and backward compatibility.

### Major Architectural Differences

| Aspect | Babylon.js | Babylon Lite |
|---|---|---|
| **Rendering API** | WebGL 1/2 + WebGPU | **WebGPU-only** — no WebGL fallback |
| **API Style** | Class-based OOP (`new Scene(engine)`) | **Plain data + functions** (`createSceneContext(engine)`) |
| **Tree-shaking** | Partial | **100% tree-shakable** — unused features cost zero bytes |
| **Scene ownership** | Objects know about the scene | **Scene is sole owner** — objects are standalone data, added via `addToScene()` |
| **Bundle size** | Large (hundreds of KB to MB) | **Fraction of Babylon.js** — measured per-scene with strict KB ceilings |
| **Build toolchain** | Various | **Vite-only** with WGSL shader minification |

### Key Technical Features
- **Frame Graph** — explicit ordered render tasks (RenderPass, RTT, overlays) instead of implicit rendering
- **Node Material Editor support** — NME snippet parser covering core, PBR, math, texture, procedural blocks
- **WGSL shaders** — all shaders written in WGSL, minified in production builds
- **Dynamic imports** — features like animation groups, PBR reflectance, etc. are only loaded when actually used
- **Pixel-identical output** — validated via Playwright visual parity tests with golden reference screenshots against Babylon.js
- **189 demo scenes** with parity tests proving visual equivalence

### Three Packages
1. **`babylon-lite`** — The core engine library (the main product)
2. **`@babylonjs/lite-compat`** — An opt-in **compatibility layer** that provides Babylon.js-shaped APIs (`new Scene()`, `new Camera()`, etc.) on top of Lite, as a migration runway. Unsupported APIs throw `LiteCompatError` so gaps are discoverable.
3. **`babylon-lite-gl`** — Placeholder for potential future WebGL support

### What's Intentionally NOT Supported (🚫)
- WebGL 1.0 / 2.0
- Classic `InstancedMesh` API (use thin instances instead)
- Full particle systems, audio, GUI, inspector, node editor
- Many Babylon.js plugins (AmmoJS, CannonJS, OBJ/STL/FBX loaders, etc.)

### What Lite Does Support Well
- PBR materials (metallic-roughness, specular-glossiness, clearcoat, sheen, anisotropy, subsurface)
- Standard materials, ShaderMaterial, GridMaterial
- glTF/.babylon/.hdr/.dds loaders + KTX/Basis compressed textures
- Shadows (ESM, PCF, cascaded)
- Skeleton animation, morph targets, vertex animation textures
- Havok Physics V2, Recast V2 navigation
- Gaussian splatting (.ply, .splat, .sog, .spz)
- CSG operations, picking, post-processing
- Device-lost recovery
- Post-process pipeline (bloom, SSAO, FXAA, DOF, chromatic aberration, etc.)
